editorial:
Imagine being nineteen years old in 1944 France, where your biggest worry is finally getting a date with the girl of your dreams. That is exactly where you find Racine. He is a first-aid worker who is mostly just looking for some fun and romance with Isabelle. When a resistance fighter shows up asking for help, Racine jumps at the chance to join the maquis. He does not do it because he is a brave soldier, but mostly to look cool in front of Isabelle. He ends up with a group of fifteen boys who are just as clueless and immature as he is. The vibe starts off light and almost playful, but you can feel the tension building as they realize they are not playing a game.

What really hits hard is how quickly the mood shifts from teenage joking to the scary reality of war. The acting feels real because the boys actually act like kids who are in over their heads. The pacing is solid, though some might find the slow build-up a bit long before the action kicks in. If you enjoy stories about losing your innocence, you should definitely check this out. It looks great in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, but if you are a collector, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical shelf is the way to go for the best picture quality.
endingExplained: The movie ends on a heartbreaking note as the reality of war destroys the boys' innocence. After the chaos of the battle, you see the brutal cost of their choices. Racine survives, but he is no longer the carefree kid from the start. The final scenes show the heavy toll of the conflict, leaving you with a sad feeling as the survivors realize that their youthful dreams are gone forever.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves historical dramas about young people in war.
